It'll sound like they're right there in the turret with you.|Han training Luke on the quad laser cannon|<ref name="The Jedi Nexus">"{{SWRadio|The Jedi Nexus}}"</ref>}} 

An '''aural sensor''', also called an '''audio interpreter'''<ref name="ELII">''[[The New Jedi Order: Enemy Lines II: Rebel Stand]]''</ref> or '''audio simulation'''<ref name="The Jedi Nexus" /> was a sensor device found on all [[Starship/Legends|spaceships]].<ref name="The Jedi Nexus" />

==Characteristics==
An aural sensor could give audio simulations of the sounds of nearby spaceships' engines and other relevant sounds while in the vacuum of space. This was done to give a spaceship's crew a rough idea of where surrounding ships were when they were not visible on a ship's screens.<ref name="The Jedi Nexus" />

==History==
The [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] was equipped with such sensors.<ref name="The Jedi Nexus" />

==Behind the scenes==
These sensors offer an [[in-universe]] explanation for why sound was heard in space in the ''Star Wars'' films despite its physical impossibility (because space contains no substance that can transmit sound waves). This phenomenon is seen in a number of science fiction films and games, not just ''Star Wars''. Sound in space is generally accepted as a cinematic convention and part of [[Wikipedia:Suspension of disbelief|suspension of disbelief]], even if it is scientifically incorrect.
